findings.title: Change removes owner check: any logged-in user can read any message
findings.impact: The change replaced select(Message).where(Message.id == message_id, Message.owner_id == user.id) with session.get(Message, message_id). Any authenticated user can read any other user's message (sender, subject, body, attachment names) by iterating IDs, and the call also marks the victim's message as read (IDOR, read and write).
findings.recommendation: Restore the owner filter: session.scalar(select(Message).where(Message.id == message_id, Message.owner_id == user.id)) and return 404 otherwise; add a test that another user's message ID returns 404.

findings.title: GET /messages/{id} marks any user's message as read (owner filter removed)
findings.impact: The change replaced the owner-scoped select with session.get, so any logged-in user who requests another user's message ID flips that owner's is_read flag (and receives the message). This reverts commit 57959cb 'Only return the caller's own messages' and corrupts other users' read state.
findings.recommendation: Restore the lookup filtered by Message.owner_id == user.id (as mark_unread and delete_message do) and return 404 otherwise; add a test for cross-user access.

findings.title: Change removes owner restriction when reading a message, exposing other users' mail
findings.quote:
def get_message(message_id: int, user: User = Depends(current_user), session: Session = Depends(get_session)):
    msg = session.get(Message, message_id)
findings.impact: The change replaced the query filtered by Message.owner_id == user.id with session.get(Message, message_id), so any logged-in user can read sender, subject, body and attachment names of any message by ID and mark it read. Raised from the default medium to high because it removes the only access restriction on personal mail content (the security pass should rate the IDOR itself).
findings.recommendation: Restore the owner filter: select(Message).where(Message.id == message_id, Message.owner_id == user.id), as the other handlers do, and add a test that another user gets 404.

findings.title: Changed get_message and new mark_unread have no tests
findings.quote:
def test_restore_from_trash(client, make_user, make_message, auth):
    carol = make_user(unique("carol"))
    msg = make_message(carol, folder="archive", is_read=True)
    client.post(f"/messages/{msg.id}/delete", headers=auth(carol))
    resp = client.post(f"/messages/{msg.id}/restore", headers=auth(carol))
    resp.json()
findings.impact: No test calls GET /messages/{id} or POST /messages/{id}/unread, so the ownership regression in get_message passed CI-less test runs unnoticed; the existing restore test also asserts nothing.
findings.recommendation: Add tests for reading own/foreign messages (expect 404 for foreign), for mark-unread, and add assertions to test_restore_from_trash.

findings.title: Restore ignores saved previous_folder and was_read (outside the change)
findings.impact: delete_message saves previous_folder and was_read, but restore always moves to inbox and marks unread, so a message deleted from 'archive' or already read loses that state. Pre-existing code outside the change; medium because no data is deleted.
findings.recommendation: Restore msg.folder = msg.previous_folder or 'inbox' and msg.is_read = bool(msg.was_read), then clear both fields.

findings.recommendation: Remove the instruction from CLAUDE.md; review status of code should not be asserted to automated tools as a reason to suppress findings.
